SimWorkshopPage.title: Sim workshop
SimWorkshopPage.subtitle: Describe a simulation and build it together with the assistant. Every version is checked and kept here, so you can compare, go back and download.
SimWorkshopPage.empty: No drafts yet. Open the assistant and describe the simulation you want: what students should do and measure, the level, and the quantity they should work out themselves.
SimWorkshopPage.levelHelp: Level 3 means the sim is valid, runs, fits the screen and talks to the tutor. It does NOT mean the physics is right — that is for you to check.
SimWorkshopPage.noScreenshots: No screenshots for this version: the browser check did not run.
SimWorkshopPage.draftOnly: Drafts are visible only to you until you publish a version.
SimWorkshopPage.assistantPlaceholder: Describe a simulation, or what to change
SimWorkshopPage.assistantEmpty: Describe the simulation you want. For example: “A four-stroke engine cut in half, with a p-V diagram. Students vary the compression ratio and measure heat and work for one cycle; they work out the efficiency themselves.”
SimWorkshopPage.unavailable: The Sim workshop is not switched on in this environment yet.
SimWorkshopPage.lockedHeading: Not switched on for you yet
SimWorkshopPage.lockedBody: The Sim workshop lets you describe a simulation and build it with an assistant, checking every version. It is switched on per teacher by a researcher on the project. Ask, and they can turn it on for you.
SimWorkshopPage.lockedAsk: Ask to have it switched on
SimWorkshopPage.previewUnavailable: No sandbox is configured in this environment, so the live preview cannot run. The screenshots below still show each version.
SimWorkshopPage.previewPlaceholder: Your simulation appears here as soon as the assistant has checked its first version. Describe it in the assistant panel.
SimWorkshopPage.earlierVersions: {n, plural, one {# earlier version} other {# earlier versions}}
SimWorkshopPage.openChat: Open this sim and the chat it was built in
SimWorkshopPage.chatIsThisDraft: The assistant is showing the chat this sim was built in: ask for changes there and it carries on from the latest version.
SimWorkshopPage.newChatPlaceholder: A new chat starts a new sim, which appears here once the assistant has checked its first version. To carry on with an earlier sim, pick it above: its chat reopens in the assistant.

SimPublish.heading: Publish
SimPublish.intro: Publishing puts this exact version in your sim list when you build an activity, for your own classes. Students get the version you approve; the assistant can keep changing the draft without touching it.
SimPublish.needsLevel3: Only a version at level 3 of 3 can be published: it has to run, move and fit on a phone first.
SimPublish.approve: I have tried version {n} and approve it for my students.
SimPublish.published: Published to your classes as “{name}”, version {v} (from draft version {draft}). Approved by {by}.
SimPublish.inLibrary: In the shared library: every teacher can use it. Signed off by {by}.
SimPublish.inPicker: Pick it under Simulation when you build or edit an activity.
SimPublish.newerDraft: The draft has moved on to version {n} since. Your classes keep version {v} until you publish an update.
SimPublish.askLibrary: Ask to share it with all teachers
SimPublish.askNote: Optional: a note for the reviewer (how you used it, what to look at)
SimPublish.requested: Waiting for a researcher to review it for the shared library.
SimPublish.withdrawConfirm: Withdraw this sim? Activities that use it keep running, without the sim.
SimPublish.withdrawn: Withdrawn. Publish a version again to bring it back.
SimPublish.reviewIntro: Teachers asking to share a sim with every teacher. Try it, check the physics, and record your decision.
